item.title: High Agency
item.description:
Author: George Mack

out of there. Who do you call?

When you’re told that something is impossible, is that the end of the conversation, or does that start a second dialogue in your mind? How to get around whoever it is that’s just told you that you can’t do something" - Eric Weinstein on high agency.

When faced with a problem, ask your brain, “Does this defy the laws of physics?” — it will reply with “No” — and begin generating ludicrous ways this could be possible. Asking your brain this question wipes your mental whiteboard around the problem and knocks on the door of your sleeping creativity.

item.title: The Pathless Path
item.description:
Author: Paul Millerd

8. Redefine Success

In 2019, Gallup surveyed Americans about success. In response to the question, “How do you personally define success?”, 97% agreed with the following statement: A person is successful if they have followed their own interests and talents to become the best they can be at what they care about most. In response to the question, “How do you think others definesuccess?”, only 8% gave the same answer. Instead, 92% felt that other people defined success as follows: A person is successful if they are rich, have a high-profile career, or are well‑known.

item.title: What Would You Do If You Weren't Afraid?
item.description:
• About Courage and Knowing myself what I would do if I didn’t Fear what I fear now.

Quotes

On purpose

The two most important days in your life are the day you are born and the day you find out why.” — Mark Twain

On potential

The first thing God said to Adam after Adam ate the forbidden fruit was a question—the first question asked since humans were created. And this is what God said: Ayeka —Genesis 3:9 Ayeka means, “Where are you?” Did God not know where Adam was? Of course He did. God was really asking if Adam knew where he was, not physically, but existentially. Where on his journey was he right now? How far had he wandered from his potential?

item.title: 101 Essays That Will Change The Way You Think
item.description:
Quotes

On Truth

Every generation has a “monoculture” of sorts, a governing pattern or system of beliefs that people unconsciously accept as “truth.”

On Planning

Your brain can only perceive what it’s known, so when you choose what you want for the future, you’re actually just recreating a solution or an ideal of the past

On beliefs

A belief is what you know to be true because experience has made it evident to you. If you want to change your life, change your beliefs. If you want to change your beliefs, go out and have experiences that make them real to you. Not the opposite way around

item.title: The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari
item.description:
Author: Robin Sharma

Life is no brief candle for me. It is a sort of splendid torch which I have got hold of for the moment, and I want to make it burn as brightly as possible before handing it on to future generations. George Bernard Shaw

It was by Winston Churchill and it spoke volumes about the man that Julian was: Sure I am that this day we are masters of our fate, that the task which has been set before us is not above our strength; that its pangs and toils are not beyond my endurance. As long as we have faith in our own cause and an unconquerable will to win, victory will not be denied us.

item.title: Principles
item.description:
Author: Ray Dalio

learned that failure is by and large due to not accepting and successfully dealing with the realities of life, and that achieving success is simply a matter of accepting and successfully dealing with all my realities.

learned that there is an incredible beauty to mistakes, because embedded in each mistake is a puzzle, and a gem that I could get if I solved it, i.e., a principle that I could use to reduce my mistakes in the future.

item.title: Getting Things Done
item.description:
GTD

GTD Intro

  • Anything that causes you to overreact or underact can control you, and often does.
  • Anything that doesn’t belong where it is, the way it is, is an “open loop”, which will be pulling on your attention if it’s not appropriately managed.
  • First of all, if it’s on your mind, your mind isn’t clear. Anything you consider unfinished must be captured in a trusted system outside your mind.
  • Research that significant part of your psyche cannot help but keep track of your open loops, and not as an intelligent, positive motivator, but as a detractor from anything else you need or want to think about.
  • As soon as you attach a “should”, “need to”, or “ought to” to an item, it becomes an incomplete.
  • Project list is not meant to hold plans or details about your projects themselves, nor should you try to keep it arranged by priority or size or urgency.
  • The calendar should show only the “hard landscape” around which you do the rest of your actions.
  • You will often have ideas that you will want to keep about projects but that are not necessarily next actions. Those ideas fall into the broad category of “PROJECT SUPPORT MATERIALS”.
  • One of the biggest problems with PMS is that they blend a few actionable things with a large amount of data and material that has value but no action attached.
  • When the non-actionable items aren’t properly managed, they clog up the whole process.
  • MAGIC KEY TO SUSTAINABILITY OF THE PROCESS IS THE WEEKLY REVIEW.
  • Project types:
    • Those that still have your attention even after you’ve determined their next actions.
    • Those about which potentially useful ideas and supportive details just show up ad hoc.
  • Sense of anxiety and guilt doesn’t come from having too much to do; it’s the automatic result of breaking agreements with yourself.
  • Use your mind to think about things, rather than think of them.

Defining anything in GTD

  1. Describe, in a single written sentence, your intended successful outcome for this problem or situation. [ INTENDED OUTCOME ]
  2. Write down the very next physical action required to move the situation forward. [ NEXT ACTION ]

Calendar

  1. Time Specific Actions.
  2. Day Specific Actions.
  3. Day Specific Information.

Tools

  1. Someday/Maybe Lists
  2. Tickler System

Reviewing Process

  1. All your PROJECTS, ACTIVE PROJECT PLANS, and NEXT ACTIONS, AGENDAS, WAITING FOR, and even SOMEDAY/MAYBE lists should be reviewed once a week.

Leveraging contexts

  1. Asking why a. Defines success. b. Creates decision-making criteria. c. Aligns resources. d. Motivates. e. Clarifies focus. f. Expands options.
  2. Capturing Tasks a. Full capturing. b. Clarifying and deciding actions for all the input you’ll want to externalize and capture.
  3. Incompletion Triggers a. Process the top item first. b. Process one item at a time. c. Never put anything back to “INBOX”.
  4. Record dates a. On everything that you hand off to others.

Hidden Projects

  1. Current activities.
  2. Higher-horizon interests.
  3. Current Problems, issues and opportunities.

Frequent Mistakes

  1. Not setting inbox to zero. ==> Mind doesn’t trust the system unless you take everything into the system. No papers, no anything.
  2. Not clarifying the next action. ==> Next task on filing taxes might be to call or email or discuss.
  3. Project List is not current. ==> People resist because it forces you to get clear on your larger commitments.
  4. Someday/Maybe List ==> Out of sight is out of mind. An active someday/maybe list gives us freedom to park commitments for later. Use this properly. Without one, they’ll linger in your mind or get stale on the projects list.
  5. Not taking out time to plan ==> If you don’t take time to plan, you’ll not be ready for the surprises.
  6. Putting everything on the calendar ==> Calendar is only meant for data and time specific actions/information.
  7. Taking too long to do the weekly review ==> Something’s wrong if it is taking > 1.5 hrs. Don’t use this time to clear the backlog.
  8. Not look at your lists ==> Looking at it regularly, mind learns to trust your GTD to track open loops.
  9. Investing in tools and not habits ==> Tool is not as important as building the right habits. a. Capture what has your attention. b. Clarify what it means. c. Organize where it belongs. d. Reflect regularly. e. Engage make a trusted choice.
  10. Addiction to Stress ==> Being present with what you are doing.

More nuances to the process

  • Inbox should be processed based on actionability of the item.
  • No task should be inside inbox for too long. It either needs to go to References list or needs to go to Actionable List.
  • When you put items into inbox, they can be more abstract such as “Plan to do something” but when they are going into Actionable list, the task needs to be visible and actionable.
  • Once it’s an actionable task, you decide whether it takes more than 2 minutes to do it. Overhead of tracking >2 min task is significant.
  • Try delegating the task before you start doing it.
  • Now, if the task is too big, it will go into a projects list.
  • The tasks that needs to be done immediately will go into NEXT ACTIONS list.
  • If there is a task where you are waiting for someone after delegation, it will be in WAITING FOR list. You will have a scheduled date where you check the status of that work with the person.

Projects

  • Deliverables/Intended Outcomes
  • Objectives
  • Descriptions
  • At least one actionable item so that it’s a WIP not stale meat.

Contexts

  • Tags to be put on next actions list.
  • Where action is to be done, what equipment you need to do it.
  • How many contexts and how many next actions depends on how your day is structured.
  • Agenda Contexts for Persons if there are meetings.

Calendar

  • Only have things that are time and date sensitive into the calendar.

Weekly Review

  • Make sure each project has at least one NEXT ACTION.
  • Make sure NEXT ACTION tasks are thos eyou really want to or need to do if you have time during the next week. Else, move it to SOMEDAY/MAYBE list.
  • Check SOMEDAY/MAYBE list to get anything back to action.

Trigger Lists

  • Simple keywords to navigate the week.

Read/Review Folder

  • Tasks that are not actual tasks but you could do it when you have some spare time to kill.

Tickler File

  • Physical Goods needed on a particular day such as tickets.

item.title: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant
item.description:
• If you’re not willing to do a wholesale , 24/7, 100 percent swap with who that person is, then there is no point in being jealous.
  • Escape competition through authenticity. Trying to do the same thing just the way someone else did won’t work great for you.
  • Happiness: Being in the moment. The fewer desires you have, the more you can accept the present.
  • Reality is neutral. The world just reflects your own feelings back at you.
  • Life isn’t hard. We make it hard. One of the words that makes it hard is the word “should”.
  • When it comes to medicines for the mind, placebo effect is 100% effective. You want to be positively inclined, not incredulous in belief. If it is fully internalized, you will have a positive mindset.
  • Use your judgment to figure out the kinds of environments you can thrive in, and then create an environment around you so you’re statistically likely to succeed.
  • The real truths are heresies. They cannot be spoken. Only discovered, whispered, and perhaps read.

Action

  • Impatient with actions, patience with results.
  • When you say, “I’m going to do this,” and “I’m going to be that,” you’re really putting it off. You’re giving yourself an out. At least if you’re self-aware, you can think, “‘I say I want to do this, but I don’t really because if I really wanted to do it, I would just do it.”
  • Anything you have to do, just get it done. Life is slipping away.

Desire

  • Desire is a contract you make with yourself to be unhappy until you get what you want.
  • Try to have only one big desire in life at one time which will be the axis of your suffering. This is the area where you have chosen to be unhappy.
  • Don’t have two - you will be distracted.
  • It’s way more important to perfect your desires than to try to do something you don’t 100 percent desire.
  • Every time you desire, ask “Is it so important to me I’ll be unhappy unless this goes my way?”

War and Peace

  • When you start a business, in a way, you’re going to war. When you struggle with your roommates as to who should clean the dishes, you’re going to war.
  • Peace is not a guarantee. It’s always flowing. You want to learn the skill of flowing with life and accepting it in most cases.
  • Successful are those who step out of the game entirely, who don’t even play the game, who rise above it. People with such internal mental and self-control and self-awareness, they need nothing from anybody else. Jerzy Gergorek - I.

Life is short

  • Anything from the past is gone. A lot of unhappiness comes from comparing things from the past to the present.
  • Believing in utter insignificance of the self helps you remove desire for the Universe to conform to your will and desire. Your life is a firefly blink in a night.
  • Understanding the futility of what you’re doing can bring great happiness and peace.
  • You are gone in three generations, and nobody cares. Before you showed up, nobody cared.

Habits

  • You have to go through life replacing your thoughtless habits with good ones.
  • Changing habits:
    1. Pick one thing.
    2. Cultivate a desire.
    3. Visualize it.
    4. Plan a sustainable path.
    5. Identify needs, triggers, and substitutes.
    6. Tell your friends.
    7. Track meticulously.
  • Self-discipline is a bridge to a new self-image.

People you are around

  • Are they upbeat?
  • Are those relationships low-maintenance?
  • Do you admire and respect but not envy them?

Conflict

  • Don’t hang around people who are constantly engaging in conflict.

Seeing the truth

  • No. 1 thing that clouds us is our preconceived notions of the way it should be.
  • Your ego doesn’t want to face the truth. The smaller you make your ego, the less desires you have for the outcome, the easier it will be to see reality.
  • Suffering is the moment when we can no longer deny reality.
  • Try to acknowledge publicly if something isn’t going well. This way you don’t delude yourself from what’s actually going on.

Importance of Foundations

  • Knowing how to be persuasive when speaking is far more important than being an expert digital marketer.

Accepting Pain

  • Write down last time such painful thing happened and how you happened to grow after years.

item.title: Steal Like an Artist
item.description:
• By copying from great artists, you start learning in a way thats real good.

Don’t look at the world looking at what’s “good” and what’s “bad”. There’s only stuff worth stealing, and stuff that’s not worth stealing.

Everything that needs to be said has already been said. But, since no one was listening, everything must be said again. – Andre Gide

“What is originality? Undetected plagiarism. " – William Ralph Inge
